> FAQs (version 3.0, 2014). Field names have been updated to the current standard; legacy
> names are shown in parentheses. DataType `P` (size-stratified subsampling) has been added
> throughout. The survey list reflects the current DATRAS holdings rather than the 2014
> snapshot. The source document is `docs_external/DATRAS_documentation/DATRAS_FAQs.pdf`.

## Overview of DATRAS

### What is DATRAS?

DATRAS is an online database of trawl surveys hosted by ICES. It stores data from
internationally coordinated fish trawl surveys in ICES area 27 in a standardised format and
provides a data quality check upon upload. The DATRAS portal offers online services for
uploading and downloading survey data.

### What can DATRAS data be used for?

DATRAS is used by ICES expert groups, national institutes, and researchers for verifying,
storing, and obtaining fisheries-independent sampling data. The data can be used in stock
assessments, biodiversity studies, and other fisheries-related projects. All data products are
accessible under ICES Data Policy.

### What is the timespan of DATRAS data?

Each survey has its own timeline. The oldest records are from 1965 (NS-IBTS). A full
overview of survey coverage, including first and last year and valid haul counts, is given in
the [D2.2 surveys table](../../deliverables/D2.2_data_formats_metadata.qmd#sec-metadata).

### Which surveys are available via DATRAS?

DATRAS currently holds data from 29 surveys covering the Northeast Atlantic (as of 2026).
The 2014 version of this document listed 15 surveys; the inventory has grown substantially.
See the D2.2 surveys table for the full current list. Surveys include NS-IBTS, BITS, BTS,
EVHOE, IE-IGFS, NIGFS, FR-CGFS, SP-NORTH, SP-PORC, SP-ARSA, PT-IBTS, and many others.

### Which data products can I get from DATRAS?

All uploaded survey data can be downloaded as raw **exchange data** (HH, HL, CA record
types). Some surveys also offer standard derived data products computed by the ICES expert
groups:

| Product | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| CPUEL | CPUE-by-length per haul |
| CPUEA | CPUE-by-age per haul |
| IDX | Survey abundance indices |
| CW | Catch weight by species |
| FL | Survey-specific flex file (additional fields) |
| LT | Marine litter assessment |

From April 2012, all data products include a `DateofCalculation` field for tracking
changes.

### How do I acknowledge use of DATRAS data?

Follow the ICES Data Policy. Example citations:

> ICES Database of Trawl Surveys (DATRAS). ICES, Copenhagen. https://datras.ices.dk

> ICES DATRAS, Extraction [DATE]. [Survey name] data [year range]. ICES, Copenhagen.
> https://datras.ices.dk

### What are the data use restrictions?

DATRAS data are available under the ICES open access data policy (adopted 2006, updated
2012). Aggregated data and raw data are freely available under these conditions.

## For Data Users

### Downloading data

#### How do I access trawl survey data?

Survey data and derived products can be downloaded from the DATRAS download page. Note
that the web portal limits downloads to 1 million records. For larger datasets, split the
download into smaller parts (e.g. by year or quarter) or use the ICES web services / {obus}
parquet access (`dr_con()`) for efficient bulk access without record limits.

#### Why are not all data products available for all surveys?

DATRAS data products are developed and verified in cooperation with the relevant ICES Expert
Groups. This is a time-consuming process, and newer surveys may not yet have derived
products. Currently CPUEL is available for 8 of the 29 surveys (BITS, EVHOE, IE-IGFS,
NS-IBTS, ROCKALL, SCOROC, SCOWCGFS, SWC-IBTS).

#### What are "Standard species"?

Standard species are the target species of a given survey. While all surveys aim to record
all species caught, each survey has one or more target species for which detailed biological
data (sex, maturity, age, individual weight) are collected. Age-based data products (CPUEA,
IDX) are therefore available only for standard species. Refer to the relevant survey manual
for the standard species list.

### Understanding the data format

#### How do I understand the DATRAS exchange file format?

Exchange data are the raw survey data as submitted by national institutes. Each file contains
three record types:

| Record | Content |
|--------|---------|
| **HH** | Haul Header — one row per haul; gear, position, timing, validity |
| **HL** | Haul-level Length — catch by length class per species per haul |
| **CA** | Catch-at-age — individual biological measurements |

The three record types share a common set of haul identification fields and are linked by the
composite haul key `.id` (constructed from `Survey`, `Year`, `Quarter`, `Country`,
`Platform` (Ship), `Gear`, `StationName` (StNo), `HaulNumber` (HaulNo)). In the raw CSV
submission format, these correspond to the first 11 fields common to all record types.

#### What does "−9" stand for?

`−9` is the DATRAS sentinel value for a missing or inapplicable field. It is not a real
measurement. In the IMBUS standardised product (`{obus}`, parquet files) all `−9` values
are replaced with proper `NA`.

#### What are haul duration, vessel speed, and trawl parameters?

Standard values for `HaulDuration` (HaulDur), vessel speed, and gear parameters are
defined in the survey manuals. Actual values as recorded during the haul are reported in the
HH record fields `HaulDuration` (HaulDur), `GroundSpeed`, `Distance`, `DoorSpread`,
`WingSpread`, and `WarpLength`.

#### Are catch figures adjusted for hauling time?

This depends on `DataType` in the HH record. See [DataType and HL field interpretation]
for details.

#### Are all species reported in DATRAS?

Surveys intend to record all species caught, but it is the responsibility of the national
data submitter whether all species are reported. The fields `SpeciesValidity` (SpecVal) in
HL (field 26 in the raw HH record) and `SpeciesCategory` (CatIdentifier) (field 27) provide
further context. Some surveys report a limited species list; refer to the survey manual.

In CA records, mainly standard survey species are reported.

#### What is `SpeciesValidity` (SpecVal)?

`SpeciesValidity` in HL records specifies how the species was handled:

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `1` | Full record: lengths, numbers, weights — **use in standard products** |
| `0` | Invalid |
| `4` | Total number only; no lengths measured |
| `5` | Presence/absence only |
| `6` | Weight only |
| `7` | Numbers and weights; no lengths |
| `10` | Lengths and numbers; no weights |

Only `SpeciesValidity == "1"` records are used in DATRAS-derived data products. Records
with other values may still be of value for biodiversity or non-standard analyses.

`SpeciesValidity` is also linked to haul validity: if the haul was invalid or used for
calibration, `SpeciesValidity` will reflect this.

#### What species reference system is used?

Species codes currently used for submissions are **WoRMS AphiaIDs** (`SpeciesCodeType`
(SpecCodeType) = `"W"`). In historical submissions ITIS TSN (`"T"`) and NODC (`"N"`) codes
were used. For cross-era analysis, all submitted codes are mapped to validated WoRMS AphiaIDs
in the field `ValidAphiaID` (Valid_Aphia / Valid_WoRMS) in HL and CA records. Always use
`ValidAphiaID` as the join key for species — never the raw `SpeciesCode` (SpecCode).

In derived data products (CPUEL, CPUEA, IDX), species are identified by valid Latin names or
AphiaIDs.

#### Where can I find species names for codes in the file?

Species names can be matched to codes via the [DATRAS Species Query Tool](https://datras.ices.dk/Data_products/qryspec.aspx)
or directly via the [WoRMS database](https://www.marinespecies.org/).

If work in R you can also try this:
```
icesVocab::findAphia(c("cod", "haddock", "saithe"))
icesVocab::findAphia("Gadus morhuha", latin = TRUE)
```


#### Where can I find information about species maximum length?

Per-survey maximum length classes (mm) are listed on the DATRAS reporting format page (DATSU). Note that this list is static and was last updated in January 2011.

#### What area codes are used in DATRAS?

Area information appears in several places:

- **Haul positions:** `ShootLatitude`/`ShootLongitude` and `HaulLatitude`/`HaulLongitude`
  in HH, reported as **decimal degrees**.
- **Statistical rectangle:** `StatisticalRectangle` (StatRec) in HH, based on shooting
  position (unless the majority of the haul was in the adjacent rectangle).
- **Depth strata:** `DepthStratum` (Stratum) in HH, for surveys with depth-stratified
  sampling.
- **Age-sampling areas:** `AreaCode` and `AreaType` in CA, indicating whether the age
  sample is haul-level (`AreaType == "H"`) or area-pooled. Always check `AreaType` before
  joining CA records to HH.

ICES statistical rectangles are described at the [ICES maps page](https://www.ices.dk/marine-data/maps/Pages/ICES-statistical-rectangles.aspx).

#### Do DATRAS data pass any quality validation?

Yes. Before upload, all files pass the **DATSU** screening utility, which applies logical,
value, and vocabulary checks. Critical errors must be corrected before the file can be
uploaded; warnings are non-critical. Weight-length outlier graphs are also provided as an
additional screening tool.

Every year, responsible expert groups review their data and report irrelevancies to the
DATRAS team. If you find erroneous data, contact DATRAS administration
(DATRASAdministration@ices.dk).

### CPUE and derived products

#### What is CPUE in DATRAS?

CPUE (catch per unit effort) in DATRAS is the catch in numbers of individuals of the same
species, adjusted to **one hour of hauling**.

#### If I compare CPUE per length values to the exchange file, they don't match. Why?

Exchange files contain data as submitted, potentially in DataType R (raw), S (sub-sampled),
or C (catch per unit effort). CPUE data products display numbers raised to one hour of
hauling. To compare, you must apply the appropriate raising formula to the exchange data.
See [DataType and HL field interpretation] for the correct formula per DataType.

#### What do zeroes mean in a CPUE product?

A CPUE value of zero means the species was **absent** from that haul but was caught by at
least one vessel in the same survey/year/quarter. Zero records are automatically added to
all hauls where the species was absent. Explicit zero rows are required for unbiased
abundance indices.

A species may also have a zero if the data submitter observed but did not record biological
data. Refer to the exchange file for details.

#### A species is missing from CPUE for some years/quarters. Why?

Records for a species in a CPUE product appear only if at least one submitter observed and
reported it in that year/quarter. If no submitter reported the species in a given
year/quarter, no records (including zeroes) will be present in the product.

#### Why are age records limited to age_6 or age_10 in age-based products?

Age-based products are designed according to requirements from the responsible ICES Expert
Group. Groups specify a **plus group** age, above which all fish are aggregated (e.g. NS-IBTS
uses plus group age 6: all fish aged 6+ are recorded as age 6).

#### What is country code DUM (DUMMY)?

Country code `DUM` was used for reporting historical age data from Danish commercial vessels
with platform codes `DCA` and `HOL` in 1983–1995.

#### Where are BITS data before 1991?

BITS started in the early 1980s but was not standardised until 1991. The responsible expert
group (WGBIFS) decided that only data from 1991 onward should be available via DATRAS.
Contact WGBIFS for access to earlier data.

#### Where do I find survey abundance indices?

DATRAS provides CPUE-by-length and CPUE-by-age products for standard species. These are
accessible via `dr_get("IDX", ...)` in {obus}. Note that no weight-based products are
currently available from DATRAS.

#### Is there a tool to convert age to weight?

Not directly. You can use the CA records (including individual weight measurements where
available) to construct your own age–weight relationship.

#### Can I see when data were last corrected?

The DATRAS Submission Status page shows when the last cruise submission was made. The
current DATRAS version does not show what was changed in a re-submission.

## For Data Submitters

### General

#### What is the deadline for my submission?

Submission deadlines are listed on the DATRAS home page. Contact DATRAS administration if
you are unsure.

#### How should my data file be formatted?

DATRAS accepts **CSV** files (comma-separated, decimal point `.`, no blank fields — use
`−9` for missing values, no headers). One file should contain all record types (HH, HL, CA)
for the same year, quarter, country, vessel, and gear. All fields from the reporting format
must be present.

#### Which units and codes should be used?

Field descriptions, units, and valid codes are in the DATRAS Reporting Format documentation
and in the ICES Vocabulary Server (https://vocab.ices.dk/). Within {obus}, valid codes are
also available via `dr_lookup_vocabulary`.

#### How do I get access to the DATRAS upload page?

Write to DATRAS administration and the Chair of the associated ICES Expert Group with your
submitter details and access request.

### Submission process

#### How do I submit my file?

Direct upload is available for most surveys from the DATRAS uploading page. Follow the
instructions in "How to upload data into DATRAS" (available in the Documents section).

#### What quality control does my file pass?

Files pass the **DATSU** screening utility before upload:

- **Critical errors** must be corrected; the file cannot be uploaded until they are
  resolved.
- **Warnings** are non-critical; the submitter decides whether to correct them.
- **Information messages** do not affect uploading.

Screening results are displayed on the DATRAS page and sent to the submitter's email. If a
screening message is unclear, click the question mark in the screening results table for
more detail. If still unclear, contact DATRAS administration with your file and a
screenshot.

#### What is error grouping in DATSU?

When the same error occurs many times, DATSU groups them into a single entry with a
count. The submitter can expand the group to see individual occurrences. This avoids
scrolling through thousands of identical messages.

#### I get "the survey selected does not include the country present in the file". What is wrong?

Check:

1. The country code matches the vocabulary at https://vocab.ices.dk/?ref=4.
2. Numbers use a decimal **point** (`.`), not a decimal comma.
3. Your account has upload rights for this survey. Contact DATRAS administration if not.

#### I cannot find my uploaded data on the download page.

Check the DATRAS Submission Status page. If your submission is listed there with the correct
upload time, the upload was successful. Updates to the download page may take a few days due
to manual quality-control processing. If the data are needed urgently, contact DATRAS
administration.

#### Can I make a partial re-submission by haul or record type?

No. DATRAS requires a complete re-submission per year, quarter, country, vessel, and gear.

#### What happens to existing data when I re-submit?

Existing data are overwritten when the data warehouse is updated. Always keep a copy of
previous submissions. Note: if you re-submit with different key values (year, quarter,
country, vessel, gear), the old data will **not** be overwritten — contact DATRAS
administration to remove duplicates.

#### Can I document what was changed in a re-submission?

Yes — use the remarks box at the final upload step. You are also welcome to email DATRAS
administration describing the corrections made.

### Technical issues for data submitters

#### DataType and HL field interpretation {#sec-datatype-faq}

`DataType` is set at the haul level (HH record) and governs how HL fields must be
interpreted. It is the most common source of silent errors when working with exchange data.

| DataType | Description | CPUE formula |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| `R` | Raw; catch sorted, some species may be sub-sampled. `SubsamplingFactor` ≥ 1 | `n_haul = Σ(NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor)` |
| `S` | Bulk unsorted catch sub-sampled before sorting. `SubsamplingFactor` > 1 | Same as R |
| `P` | Size-stratified subsampling — different `SubsamplingFactor` per size grade. **Do not sum `TotalNumber` across strata.** | Same row-level formula as R, applied per stratum |
| `C` | Catch pre-raised to 1 hour of hauling. `SubsamplingFactor` = 1 | `n_hour = NumberAtLength`; `n_haul = NumberAtLength × HaulDuration / 60` |

The `{obus}` function `dr_HL_standardised()` applies the correct formula for all DataTypes
automatically. For full field-by-field specifications and empirical notes on DataType
misuse in submissions, see
[DATRAS Technical Reference §DataType](DATRAS_Technical_Reference.qmd#sec-datatype).

#### What is `SpeciesCategory` (CatIdentifier), and how do I use it?

`SpeciesCategory` (CatIdentifier) is the ID assigned to a size- or weight-based subsampling
stratum for a given species and sex within a haul. It is used when a truly representative
sub-sample cannot be selected from the whole catch — for example, when larger fish are
sorted away and measured separately with a different sub-sampling factor.

- Assign `SpeciesCategory = 1` to the first stratum and `SpeciesCategory = 2`, `3`, ... to
  additional strata (up to 5 per species per haul).
- If no size categorisation was applied, use `SpeciesCategory = 1` throughout.
- Reporting different **sex** categories for the same species does not require different
  `SpeciesCategory` values — keep `SpeciesCategory = 1` and vary `SpeciesSex` (Sex) instead.

See the NS-IBTS survey manual (section "Length composition") for worked examples.

#### How is Day/Night defined?

Daytime is defined as the period from 15 minutes before sunrise to 15 minutes after sunset,
following NOAA's solar calculations. The derived field `DayNight` in HH is populated by
the ICES datacenter from the shooting position and time.

#### Which area/position should I report?

- **Coordinates:** `ShootLatitude`/`ShootLongitude` and `HaulLatitude`/`HaulLongitude` in
  HH, as **decimal degrees**.
- **Statistical rectangle:** `StatisticalRectangle` (StatRec) in HH, based on shooting
  position.
- **Depth strata:** `DepthStratum` (Stratum) in HH, if sampling is depth-stratified.
- **CA area codes:** `AreaCode` and `AreaType` in CA, specifying haul-level vs. area-pooled
  age sampling.

#### How do I submit area-based CA data without corresponding HL data?

CA records must always be related to a parent HL record. If age sampling was area-based,
create a **dummy HL record** by duplicating fields 2–12 from the CA record and setting all
other HL fields to `−9`.

Example CA record:
```
CA,1,SCO,SCO3,GOV,60,-9,P,S01,1,2010,W,126417,2,3,0,140,U,-9,-9,3,1,-9
```
Corresponding dummy HL record:
```
HL,1,SCO,SCO3,GOV,60,-9,P,S01,1,2010,W,126417,0,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9
```

#### Species codes and `SpeciesCodeType` (SpecCodeType)

Current submissions use WoRMS AphiaIDs (`SpeciesCodeType = "W"`). Historical data used
ITIS TSN (`"T"`) and NODC (`"N"`) codes. All codes are mapped to current WoRMS AphiaIDs in
the field `ValidAphiaID` (Valid_Aphia / Valid_WoRMS). For all analysis, use `ValidAphiaID`
as the species join key.

## Annex I: DataType examples in exchange data {#sec-annex-datatype}

### HH record: DataType values

| DataType | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `S` | Sub-sampled: catch sub-sampled before sorting; all `SubsamplingFactor` (SubFactor) values > 1 |
| `R` | Recorded by haul: catch sorted; some species may be sub-sampled; `SubsamplingFactor` ≥ 1 |
| `P` | Size-stratified (pseudocategory): different `SubsamplingFactor` per size stratum within a species; uses `SpeciesCategory` (CatIdentifier) to label strata |
| `C` | CPUE: data pre-raised to one hour of hauling; all `SubsamplingFactor` = 1 |

### HL record: field definitions

| Field (new name) | Old name | Description |
|-----------------|----------|-------------|
| `SubsamplingFactor` | SubFactor | Sub-sampling factor by haul, species, sex, and `SpeciesCategory` |
| `NumberAtLength` | HLNoAtLngt | Number of fish measured in the (sub-)sample at this length class |
| `SubsampledNumber` | NoMeas | Sum of `NumberAtLength` across length classes, by haul × species × sex × `SpeciesCategory` |
| `TotalNumber` | TotalNo | `SubsamplingFactor` × `SubsampledNumber` (DataType R/S/P); raised count per hour (DataType C) |

### Example 1: DataType S — 1,140 fish, 3 species

```
Catch: 1,140 fish   SubsamplingFactor = 2
→ Measure 570 fish (sub-sample)

  400 Plaice          150 Whiting         20 Cod
  SubFactor = 2       SubFactor = 8       SubFactor = 1
  NoMeas = 200        NoMeas = 75/2 = ...  NoMeas = 20
  Measure 200         Measure sub-sample   Measure all 20
```

For Plaice:  
`TotalNumber` = 400, `SubsamplingFactor` = 2, `SubsampledNumber` = 200  
Verify: 400 = 200 × 2 ✓  
`NumberAtLength` values sum to 200 (= `SubsampledNumber`) ✓

### Example 2: DataType R — size-stratified (DataType P encoding)

Species with two size grades in one haul:

| `SpeciesCategory` (CatIdentifier) | Size range | `SubsamplingFactor` (SubFactor) | Fish measured | `TotalNumber` (TotalNo) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Small (100–160 mm) | 5.9 | 61 | ≈ 360 |
| 2 | Large (210–420 mm) | 1.0 | 168 | 168 |

Correct haul total: **360 + 168 = 528 fish**  
Formula: `n_haul = Σ(NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor)` applied row by row — correct
for all DataTypes including size-stratified R and P hauls.  
**Do not sum `TotalNumber` across `SpeciesCategory` strata** — it is the stratum total.

## IMBUS Additions {#sec-imbus-additions}

The questions below were not in the original ICES FAQ. They arose from exploratory analysis
of the DATRAS exchange tables conducted as part of IMBUS WP2.

### What do HL records with a missing `LengthClass` represent? {#sec-lc-na}

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
**[IMBUS]** This question was not in the original ICES FAQ. It arose from IMBUS WP2
exploratory analysis of the DATRAS HL table.
:::

In the HL exchange table, records where `LengthClass` is `NA` (encoded as `−9` in raw CSV
files) are **catch-totals rows**. They record aggregate catch information for a species within
a haul but carry no individual length measurement. Every such row also has
`NumberAtLength = NA`. They are distinct from length-frequency rows in both purpose and
content.

Catch-totals rows typically carry one or more of:

| Field | Content |
|-------|---------|
| `TotalNumber` | Total count of fish in the haul (raised; or per hour for DataType C) |
| `SubsampledNumber` | Number of fish actually handled or weighed |
| `SpeciesCategoryWeight` | Catch weight for the species/category |
| `SubsamplingFactor` | Raising factor (may be 1 if all fish were counted) |

These rows arise in two situations:

1. **Species measured by count or weight only** — where `SpeciesValidity` ≠ 1 (e.g. `4` =
   total number only, `6` = weight only, `7` = numbers and weights but no lengths). In this
   case the catch-totals row *is* the only HL record for that species.
2. **Companion summary rows** — present alongside a full length-frequency series for the same
   species/haul (typically `SpeciesValidity = 1`). The catch-totals row then summarises what
   the length rows describe individually.

**Key implication for analysis:** always filter `!is.na(LengthClass)` (and
`!is.na(NumberAtLength)`) before computing CPUE or length distributions. Catch-totals rows
cannot be raised via `sum(NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor)` — they carry no
`NumberAtLength`. The `{obus}` function `dr_add_n_and_cpue()` handles this automatically.

`TotalNumber` in catch-totals rows is useful as a cross-check against the raised sum from
the length-frequency rows, but note that its scope (all-sex total vs. sex-specific) is not
consistent across surveys; see the [DATRAS data issues](issues.qmd#sec-totalnumber-reconciliation)
for a survey-by-survey reconciliation.

```{r}
#| label: lc-na-summary
#| echo: false
library(tidyverse)
library(obus)

# Confirm that all NA-LengthClass rows also have NA NumberAtLength,
# and show which aggregate fields are populated.
dr_con("HL") |>
  filter(is.na(LengthClass)) |>
  summarise(
    n_records               = n(),
    n_NA_NumberAtLength     = sum(is.na(NumberAtLength)),
    n_has_TotalNumber       = sum(!is.na(TotalNumber)),
    n_has_SubsampledNumber  = sum(!is.na(SubsampledNumber)),
    n_has_SpeciesCatWeight  = sum(!is.na(SpeciesCategoryWeight))
  ) |>
  collect()
```

### What is the difference between DataType "P" and "R"? {#sec-p-vs-r}

**Short answer:** DataType **R** (raw catch) is for hauls where the entire catch is sorted and some species are sub-sampled at a **single** rate. DataType **P** (pseudocategory) is for hauls where the catch is sorted into **multiple size grades**, each with its own sub-sampling rate.

**When you would encounter each:**

| DataType | Scenario | Sub-sampling approach |
|---|---|---|
| **R** | Regular haul | One species, one sub-sample rate per species |
| **P** | Size-stratified | One species, **multiple size grades**, each grade sub-sampled separately |
| **S** | Bulk sub-sample | Entire catch sub-sampled before sorting |
| **C** | Pre-raised | Lab already converted to CPUE (per hour) |

**Example: same species, two size grades in one haul**

| DataType | `SpeciesCategory` | Size range | `SubsamplingFactor` | Measured | `TotalNumber` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P** | 1 | Small (100–160 mm) | 5.9 | 61 | ≈ 360 |
| | 2 | Large (210–420 mm) | 1.0 | 168 | 168 |

For both P and R, calculate haul total identically: `n_haul = Σ(NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor)` per row = (61 × 5.9) + (168 × 1.0) = 528 fish.

**Why the distinction exists:**

- **DataType P explicitly signals** that size-stratification is present, so downstream users understand that multiple `SpeciesCategory` rows per species per haul are expected, and each `TotalNumber` corresponds to a size stratum.
- **DataType R** signals that there is one sub-sampling rate per species; users can be confident that summing by species will yield the haul total.

**Recommended practice for users:**
- Always use the row-level formula: `n_haul = Σ(NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor)` per haul and species
- The `{obus}` function `dr_add_n_and_cpue()` handles all DataTypes correctly


### Why do we have more than one value for SpeciesValidity within the same tow (.id) for the same species?

`SpeciesValidity` is a **record type** field — it describes *what kind of data* is present
for a species within a haul, not whether the haul is valid. The HL exchange format allows more
than one record type for the same species and haul, and some surveys use this deliberately.

A typical scenario: a species was fully length-measured (`"1"`, full record), but the crew
also recorded a total count for a size group that was not individually measured (`"4"`, total
number only), or noted a presence/absence for bycatch (`"5"`). Both rows share the same
`.id × aphia` group, so `SpeciesValidity` is not constant within that group.

This is **intentional, not an error**. BTS and Can-Mar are the main surveys that submit
multiple record types for the same species and haul. Across all surveys, ~2,786 of ~2.6
million HL groups (0.1%) show this pattern. The most common co-occurrences are `{1, 5}` and
`{4, 7}`.

**Worked example.** The following rows are taken directly from haul
`BTS:2024:3:BE:1186:BT4S:40:1` for *Sepia officinalis* (aphia 141444, common cuttlefish).
Only the `DevelopmentStage = NA` rows are shown (the egg rows, `DevelopmentStage = "E"`,
follow the same pattern):

| `LengthClass` | `NumberAtLength` | `TotalNumber` | `SpeciesValidity` |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 10 | 1 | 18 | **1** |
| 15 | 1 | 18 | **1** |
| 20 | 2 | 18 | **1** |
| 25 | 6 | 18 | **1** |
| … | … | 18 | **1** |
| 110 | 1 | 18 | **1** |
| `NA` | `NA` | 18 | **5** |

The ten `SpeciesValidity = "1"` rows carry the full length-frequency distribution
(`LengthClass` 10–110 mm, `NumberAtLength` filled). The final row, `SpeciesValidity = "5"`,
is a supplementary presence/absence marker: it carries no length or count data of its own
(`LengthClass = NA`, `NumberAtLength = NA`) but coexists in the same `.id × aphia` group.
This is the **intended semantics** of `SpeciesValidity = "5"` as defined in the DATRAS format.

**Can-Mar exception.** Can-Mar uses `SpeciesValidity = "5"` differently — on rows that
carry actual `LengthClass` and `NumberAtLength` values. Across 535 Can-Mar groups with both
`"1"` and `"5"` rows containing length data, 42% have entirely distinct length classes
between the two record types (the `"5"` rows add lengths not in the `"1"` rows), 20% are
full duplicates, and 38% partially overlap. The reason for this split is not documented
in the DATRAS submission format. Filtering to `SpeciesValidity == "1"` in Can-Mar will
therefore discard real length data in at least 42% of these groups. See
[Can-Mar SpeciesValidity="5" anomaly](#sec-canmar-specval) in the issues document.

**Practical implication:** if you aggregate over `.id × aphia` without also grouping on
`SpeciesValidity`, rows from different record types will be silently mixed together.
For most surveys (including BTS), **filter to `SpeciesValidity == "1"` before aggregating**
to retain only the full length-frequency records. For Can-Mar, the appropriate treatment
of `SpeciesValidity = "5"` rows with length data is currently unresolved.

See the [SpeciesValidity vocabulary](#vocab-specval) in D2.2 for the full code list, and
[HL grouping key constancy violations](#sec-specval-variation) in the issues document for
per-survey statistics.
